strengths: Clear and well-motivated RICH hypothesis that addresses a specific gap in Zaremba et al. (2025)
Comprehensive experimental design testing across multiple dimensions: models, attack types, budgets, and scaling approaches
Consistent empirical support for the 'rich-get-richer' effect across Sections 4.1-4.4 with appropriate statistical testing
Insightful visualizations (Figure 1 with attention maps) demonstrating how robust models better follow instructions on OOD data
Novel experimental protocols with explicit security specifications and white-box multimodal attacks
Practical guidance for combining train-time and test-time defenses for synergistic benefits
weaknesses: Limited scope: experiments on VLMs only; frontier model results (Table 4) show no significant benefits for Llama and marginal benefits for Qwen, undermining generality claims
Disconnect from original work: uses naive specification repetition rather than reasoning-based scaling, limiting direct comparison and practical applicability

Insufficient mechanistic explanation: invokes compositional generalization without rigorously explaining why base robustness enables instruction-following on OOD data; lacks investigation of representations

Confounded variable in Section 4.3: reducing ε to help non-robust models fundamentally weakens attacks, making it unclear whether benefits derive from compositional generalization or simply weaker attacks
Limited attack strength: PGD runs 100-300 iterations without comparison to stronger adaptive attacks (AutoAttack); unclear if perturbation budgets are sufficiently challenging
Modest novelty: core finding (robust models benefit more from robustness improvements) is expected; incremental contribution relative to established adversarial robustness literature
Missing ablations on prompt formulation sensitivity and alternative inference-compute scaling strategies beyond naive repetition
Frontier model failure: results in Table 4 contradict RICH predictions for large-scale VLMs, raising questions about generalizability

strengths: Well-motivated RICH hypothesis with clear empirical predictions supported by exploratory findings; comprehensive testing across multiple models (various LLaVA variants, large-scale VLMs), attack types (black-box, white-box, gradient-based), and inference-compute methods

Strong empirical validation showing consistent rich-get-richer effects: security specs help only robust models (Table 2), benefits scale with base robustness (Figure 4), and attack-budget reduction enables benefits in less-robust models (Section 4.3), with appropriate statistical testing

Insightful practical contributions: lightweight adversarial finetuning enables inference-compute benefits; Figure 2 demonstrates novel observation that attacks become more interpretable/geometrically meaningful for robust models; demonstrates robustness benefits without extensive RL finetuning

Thorough experimental design with good controls: pre-filling experiments isolate specification effects, random-token controls verify content matters, ablations in appendices test variants, multiple attack budgets validate RICH predictions

Clarifies important gap in prior work: explains why Zaremba et al. (2025)'s reasoning approach fails on vision attacks and provides actionable guidance for synergistic train-time and test-time defense combinations
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: RICH hypothesis is relatively straightforward and builds heavily on existing concepts (compositional generalization, adversarial training, security specifications); the proposed mechanism is assumed rather than rigorously demonstrated through direct measurement

Critical limitation on frontier models: large-scale VLMs (Llama-3.2-Vision-90B, Qwen-2.5-VL-72B) show NO significant benefits on adversarial Attack-Bard data (Table 5); frontier model results show o1-v achieves only 61% vs. robust VLMs performing better, severely limiting practical impact

Compositional generalization mechanism not proven: paper relies on compositional generalization as explanatory mechanism but provides no direct evidence, probing experiments, or representation analysis; connection between base robustness and compositional ability is inferred rather than established

Inference-compute scaling is unsophisticated: main approach is naive specification repetition; no comparison with more sophisticated reasoning methods; claim that RL finetuning is unnecessary seems to underutilize reasoning potential; InternVL gains are modest (≈6% improvement)

Mixed results limit confidence: LLaVA-v1.5 shows no significant CoT benefit on adversarial Attack-Bard data (p=4.2e-2); results strongest only for smaller, adversarially-trained models; benefits degrade significantly at high attack budgets, suggesting narrow applicability

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: lacks theoretical analysis of why base robustness enables compositional generalization; no exploration of alternative explanations; no analysis of fundamental limits; insufficient investigation of why large-scale models fail to benefit

Limited experimental scope: primarily vision attacks on VLMs; doesn't evaluate text jailbreaks that motivated Zaremba et al.; specific perturbation budgets tested; small sample sizes in some experiments (2 replicates); model-scale effects not fully disentangled
